# Shift offer: from any template, module or product to an offer that names the result

*Template created 2026-10-27 by Evolver from PST 173 (Sasha, 2026-10-27: «Зная какой шаблон мы используем, это идеальный способ продать что-то — напрямую назвать (и предложить!) гарантированный результат!»). Written for a founder-led transformation business like ours: a library of technologies, templates as products, a game with modules, paid sessions and a Mastermind. One open fork (what "guaranteed" means, §6) is Sasha's and is not decided here.*

## 1. Essence
**We sell shifts, not content.** The offer sounds like «Ты увидишь… и сделаешь…» / "You will see… and you will…", never "you will get a course". Because every template already names the shift it carries ([meta-template.md](./meta-template.md) §2b), we can name the result directly and promise exactly what the path delivers. **No shift, no promise.**

## 2. Principles (from the BE/DO cycle, meta-template §2b)
1. **Technology is the shift, template is the path.** The offer quotes the shift (BE) and stands on the path (DO). If either is missing, there is no offer yet.
2. **«Shift carried» is the source of the offer.** Read the template's «Shift carried» line first; the offer is that line, said to the buyer in their words.
3. **Measured by the shift that happened, not by what was delivered.** A finished course that moved nobody kept no promise; a rough session that moved one person did.
4. **The check is the person's, never ours.** An observable sign: their own words, a choice they made, a victory and its 1–10 rating, a real act in the world.
5. **Craft is honest.** A template that carries no shift is sold as a skill or a service, with no transformation promised.
6. **Knowledge multiplies itself.** Each delivered offer is a use of the template; what the check shows goes back into the template, and a new law it reveals is a library candidate (meta-template §7.8).

## 3. The offer sheet (fill one per template, module or product)
```
## Shift offer: <product / module name, as the buyer sees it>
- Template used: <docs/templates/… or module, route>
- Technology carried: PST N <name> | Craft: <the skill it is>
- Point A (their words): <what they see and feel now, as they would say it>
- Point B — they will SEE: <the new seeing, one sentence>
- Point B — they will DO: <one real step they take, inside or right after>
- Offer line (EN): You will see <…> and you will <…>.
- Offer line (RU): Ты увидишь <…> и сделаешь <…>.
- Promise (only what the path reliably delivers and they can verify): <…>
- Guarantee form: <strict shift | money-back style: see §6, Sasha's fork>
- Check (how we both know B happened): <observable sign + where it is recorded>
- Price logic: <depth of shift → price band, §7>
- Gap: <what is missing for a measurable B, if anything>
```

## 4. How to fill it
1. **Template used + technology carried.** Name the template (file or module and route) and copy its «Shift carried» number and name. If the template has none, decide honestly: name a shift it really carries, or write **Craft**. Do not force a technology to make the sheet look complete.
2. **Point A in their words.** Use the exact words people say on calls, in reviews, in the free assessment ("I do a hundred things and can't say what I do"). Not our diagnosis, not playbook language.
3. **Point B as seeing + doing.** *See:* what becomes visible that was not (a pattern, a gap, a cost, a name). *Do:* one real step that follows (they send a message, name a price, book, commit). Seeing without a step is not yet a shift you can sell; a step without new seeing is a task.
4. **The offer line.** «Ты увидишь… и сделаешь…» / "You will see… and you will…". One sentence, plain language, the buyer's words. It is the Intro headline and button of the module ([module-form.md](./module-form.md) §3), the page headline, and the last line of the call.
5. **Promise.** Only what the path *reliably* delivers, and only what the person can *verify themselves*. Good: "you will name the gap yourself", "your body will say 9 or more out of 10 to your own one-sentence business", "you will have one real booking in your calendar". Not good: "you will make $10k", "you will find your purpose" (unverifiable or not reliably ours).
6. **Check.** The sign, who sees it and where it is recorded (the victory and its 1–10 in the save file; their words in the reflection message; the booking in the calendar; the CRM after the call).
7. **Price** (§7) and **Craft honesty** (§8).

## 5. Writing rules for the offer line
- Start from B, not from the format: "You will see…", never "In this 2-hour session…". The format goes in the small print.
- Their words for A, our precision for B, one verb for the step.
- No numbers we cannot stand behind; no "guaranteed transformation" without the check beside it.
- The line must survive being said out loud on a call without embarrassment.
- One line per product. If it needs two, it is two products or one is Craft.

## 6. Guarantee: decided, none
**Decision (Sasha, 2026-10-28): no guarantee, neither money-back nor pay-after-recognition.** Recognition can be blocked by the client's own resistance (the shadow shows up as resistance and lowers resonance), so a guarantee would hand the verdict to that resistance and put Sasha in the position of justifying himself. Instead: an honest promise of what the session does, and the free 45-minute Direction Call as the readiness filter. Removed from /ignite and /founder-market-fit on 2026-10-28. Shift Offers promise the shift and its self-check as a quality standard, never as a money guarantee. The two readings below stay as the dated record of the fork.

| | A. Guaranteed = the checkable shift | B. Guaranteed = money-back style |
|---|---|---|
| **What we promise** | that the named, self-checkable B happens (they name the gap, body 9+/10, a real booking) | the same B, plus: if B does not happen by the named check, they don't pay or get the money back |
| **Strength** | clean and true; no money mechanics; fits free modules and the game | strongest buying signal; puts our skin in the game (PST 102); already live on the $555 session: "If you don't leave with a one-sentence business you recognize as yours: you don't pay" ([session-script.md](./session-script.md) §4.4) |
| **Risk** | "guaranteed" can sound like a claim without consequence | needs a clear check and refund flow for each paid product; touches checkout and refunds |
| **Fits** | free modules, the game Journey, content | paid sessions, the Mastermind, the Oracle Reading |

A mixed reading (A everywhere, B only on paid doors) is possible; that is also Sasha's call.

## 7. Price logic: by depth of shift, not volume of content
| Depth | What shifts | Typical form | Price band (current examples) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Glimpse** | one new seeing in minutes | a free module, a test, a post | free (Top Talent test, game modules) |
| **Seeing + one step** | a named result and one real act | a deep reveal, a single guided step | small ($37 Oracle Reading) |
| **Held shift** | the seeing descends into the body and changes what they do for a week or more | a group container, a practice | mid ($222 Mastermind) |
| **Full recognition** | the person leaves with their own business in one sentence and has acted on it | 1:1 session | high ($555, 2 h session) |

- More hours, more modules or more pages never raise the band; a deeper, verified shift does.
- A cheaper path to the same shift is a better product, not a cheaper one: keep the price at the depth.
- Changing live prices or checkout is outside this template (Stripe stays with Sasha).

## 8. Craft honesty: no shift, no promise
- If the template carries no shift (a spec, a production line, a tool), write **Craft** and sell it as a skill or service: what it produces, how fast, at what quality. No "you will see".
- If a module has a shift but no measurable B yet, write the **gap** and hold back the promise until a check exists. The offer line may still be used as an invitation, not as a promise.
- A promise we cannot check is not made, however good it sounds.

## 9. After delivery
- Record the check (victory + 1–10, the person's words, the real act) where the template says.
- If B did not happen: note why in the template (meta-template §7.4), and if the money-back reading applies, honour it.
- If the delivery revealed a new law, bring it to Sasha as a library candidate (meta-template §7.8).

## 10. Open edges
- The guarantee fork (§6), Sasha's.
- Per paid product: the exact check and, if B is chosen, the refund flow.
- Which offer lines go on live pages: wired by the game loop and page owners, not by this template.
